title: Exam F1RET: Pension Funding and Regulation
name: Pension Funding and Regulation
intro: The aim of this exam is for candidates to develop the following skills:
1. Understand the main provisions, principles, regulation, professional standards, governance, and techniques of funding and administration applicable to retirement benefits.
2. Apply these principles and techniques within the context of pension plans.

3. Evaluate hypothetical scenarios, including using judgment to assess the implications of possible actions and to develop appropriate proposals or recommendations relating to the funding and administration of pension plans.

Exams are administered as an open-book, four-hour exam requiring analysis in the context of a problem and submission of written responses to specific questions. Candidates will complete the exam through the CIA’s learning management system. The ranges of weights (expressed in parentheses) attached to the examination topics further below apply to most of exams administered. Candidates should also recognize that questions often cover multiple learning objectives, including communication.

outcomes.text: Define principal terms used in the funding and regulatory environment of retirement benefits. (A1).

Describe and analyze the structure of the following plan types: (C4)
bullets: b. Defined contribution and savings plans.
e. Other alternative retirement plans such as shared-risk plans, target-benefit plans, and jointly sponsored pension plans.

outcomes.text: Perform periodic valuations of ongoing plans, calculating normal cost, actuarial liability, and gains and losses, using a variety of cost methods: (C3)
bullets: a. Unit credit and projected unit credit.

outcomes.text: Compare and contrast methods described in 2. and determine their appropriateness factoring in the plan sponsor’s objectives and regulatory requirements. (D5)

Describe and apply applicable agreements respecting multi-jurisdictional pension plans between provincial regulators. (C5)
Recognize, define, interpret, apply, calculate, and evaluate minimum standards in respect of the following provisions of registered pension plans: (C5)
bullets: b. Retirement benefit formula (uniform accrual and integration with government benefits).
c. Employer cost (50 percent cost rule).
d. Interest credited on member contributions.
e. Termination benefits such as commuted values.
j. Pension credit splitting upon marriage breakdown.
m. Statement for members (annual or at retirement/termination).
r. Statutory required benefits (such as grow-in benefits in Ontario).

outcomes.text: Produce funding requirements under applicable provincial and federal minimum standard legislation considering: (C6)
bullets: d. Plan mergers and asset transfers.
g. Use of letters of credit.
j. Stabilization provisions and smoothing techniques.

outcomes.text: Apply, analyze, and evaluate the following: (C5)
bullets: b. Plan mergers and asset transfers.
h. Use of letters of credit.
i. Use of solvency reserves account.

outcomes.text: Outline the following different filing requirements and reports, including: (B2)
bullets: b. Actuarial Valuation Report and Actuarial Information Summary (AIS).
c. Pension Benefits Guarantee Fund (PBGF) Assessment.

e. Relevant policies and guidance from pension regulators.

outcomes.text: Apply and analyze rules and provisions outlined in the following: (C3)
bullets: a. Income Tax Act and Regulations (pension/retirement savings sections only);
b. Information circulars, FAQs, and interpretation bulletins (pension-related only);

d. CRA pension-related forms and guides;

i. Pension adjustment (PA), past-service pension adjustment (PSPA), and pension adjustment reversal (PAR);
k. Limits on registered defined benefit plan benefits;
r. Multi-employer pension plans (MEPPs) and specified multi-employer plans (SMEPs);

t. Group RRSP/deferred profit-sharing plan (DPSP)/employee profit-sharing plan (EPSP)/tax-free savings account (TFSA)/supplemental executive retirement plan (SERP)/retirement compensation arrangement (RCA); and

topics.title: Professionalism and standards of practice relative to plan funding

outcomes.text: Apply the standards related to communications to plan sponsors and others with an interest in an actuary’s results (i.e., participants, auditors, etc.). (C3)
Explain and apply the professional conduct guidelines. (B3)
Explain and apply relevant qualification standards. (B3)
Demonstrate compliance with requirements regarding the actuary’s responsibilities to participants, plan sponsors, etc. (B2)
Explain and apply all of the applicable standards of practice related to valuing pension benefits. (C3)
Recognize situations and actions that violate or compromise standards or professional conduct guidelines. (B2)
Recommend a course of action to repair a violation of standards or professional conduct guidelines. (D6)
Outline differences between pension commuted values and capitalized value for marriage-breakdown purposes. (B2)
Consider, assess, and decide on provisions for adverse deviations (PfADs) or statutory margins in going-concern valuations. (C5)
Describe and apply the techniques used in the development of going-concern economic and demographic assumptions. (C5)
Calculate and develop incremental cost on a hypothetical wind-up or solvency basis, sensitivity analysis, and plausible adverse scenarios. (C3)
Outline and apply CIA Guidance on Asset Valuation Methods. (C3)
Interpret and apply CIA Consolidated Standards of Practice, educational notes, and guidance provided by relevant CIA committees. (C3)
